clue.text: One with top prize is to fade away

parts.note: one as a single item is A
a trophy is the prize awarded to a winner

explanation.surface: Someone who has won the top award is now destined to fade into obscurity.
explanation.definitionFit: To atrophy is to waste or wither, as an unused muscle gradually dwindles.

clue.text: Words on the river conveying what one can feel

parts.note: a text is a body of written words
the Ure is a Yorkshire river much used in crosswords

explanation.surface: Something written about a river that conveys sensation to the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the river after the words in this down entry; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Texture is the feel of a surface to the touch, so it is literally what one can feel.

clue.text: When one goes into a very large peaceful area

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a clothing size
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A remark about the moment someone enters a vast tranquil region.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis, literally a fertile spot in a desert, figuratively means a calm refuge.

clue.text: Element of buzz about one fan, disorderly

indicators.note: the buzzing word goes round the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: a hum is a low buzzing sound

indicators.note: something disorderly is jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A chaotic fan generates a buzzing sound around itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' is the definition: a chemical element. The anagram of one-fan gives AFNI, which sits inside the buzz.
explanation.definitionFit: Hafnium is a metallic chemical element, number 72 in the periodic table.

clue.text: The salt is sprinkled in underhand action

indicators.note: salt being sprinkled is scattered about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Salt is being shaken over food in a sneaky manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secret, furtive behaviour, the manner of something done on the sly.

clue.text: Quake possibly more in extremes of terror

indicators.note: one set of letters is placed inside the other
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
possibly signals that the word more may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: An earthquake might bring yet more of the most intense fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MORE into REMO, which goes 'in' TR, the first and last letters of 'terror'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking of the ground, a small earthquake, so quake is a direct synonym.

clue.text: We probably can put up with his plans

definitions.text: We probably can put up with his plans

parts.words: We probably can put up with his plans
parts.note: read as 'we can erect a building using his drawings', the man is the professional who designs buildings rather than someone we tolerate

explanation.surface: We can probably tolerate this man and his schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like tolerate; here it means build with.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect draws up the plans from which builders construct a building.

clue.text: Mocked the golfer's item brought to one's attention

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golfer rests the ball on
to pay heed is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A golfer's peg was pointed out and laughed at.
explanation.definitionFit: To tee-hee is to snigger, so someone who tee-heed laughed mockingly.

clue.text: Nationally, it's been holding things back in the past

definitions.text: Nationally, it's been holding things back in the past

parts.words: Nationally, it's been holding things back in the past
parts.note: read as a national institution that has kept hold of things from the past, a museum for the nation, rather than one obstructing progress

explanation.surface: A complaint that the country has long been held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding things back' suggests obstruction; it means keeping old objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Museum in London is the national collection of antiquities and historic objects.

clue.text: Former partners' costs

definitions.meaning: former spouses or lovers, plural; the possessive is surface dressing

explanation.surface: What one's former spouses end up costing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exes are ex-partners, and exes is also British slang for expenses or costs.

clue.text: Fellow with the red face not entirely embarrassed? Unconvincing!

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so these letters are mixed up
not entirely means the word face loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A man with a flushed face who is only partly embarrassed seems hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' looks like the definition beside red face, but it is the anagram signal; the question-marked last word defines. The jumble makes ARFETCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far-fetched is implausible and stretches belief, hence unconvincing.

clue.text: Is mule prepared for this mixture of oats etc?

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up, so these letters are made up into a new word

explanation.surface: A question whether a mule has been readied for some breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast mix of rolled oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: One going round the back of more than one watch

definitions.text: One going round the back of

parts.note: two is more than one
a watch is a timer

explanation.surface: Something that circles behind two or more watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round the back of' means deceiving a partner behind their back.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer is unfaithful, secretly going behind a partner's back with someone else.

clue.text: Drill on ship I failed, say. A no-hoper?

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercise drill
SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: say signals a word heard spoken, a homophone

parts.note: to have missed is to have failed to hit

explanation.surface: Someone who flunked drill on board ship is called hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist always expects the worst, someone without hope of success.

clue.text: Whiskers mostly provide storage for meal pieces!

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: sideboards are side whiskers, sideburns, in British usage

explanation.surface: Beards somehow offer a place to store bits of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Sideboards is a British term for sideburns.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a dining-room cabinet holding plates, cutlery and serving dishes.

clue.text: The money available

explanation.surface: Cash that is on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The ready' is British slang for ready money, and ready also means available for use.

clue.text: One's home in the Kent area's good for gardening

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
a pad is slang for one's home or flat

explanation.surface: Someone's house in Kent is in a region with fine soil for growing things.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in southeast England, SE. The definition is a description: the tool is useful for gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade is the digging tool used for turning soil in the garden.

clue.text: Stipulate price on new video

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of video

explanation.surface: A demand for the cost of a new film to be specified.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide that something is done is to stipulate it in a contract.

clue.text: Backing the motorway's incomplete objective

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
partial means not complete

explanation.surface: Support for the motorway's unfinished aim.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 motorway runs from London to Leeds; 'Backing' turns MI into IM.
explanation.definitionFit: An impartial judgement is objective, free from bias.

clue.text: Paris excited about greeting for flier

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wrap round the greeting
excited means stirred up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Paris is thrilled, waving hello to an aviator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges PARIS into AIRSP, which goes 'about' HI.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a craft that flies, so it is one sense of flier.

clue.text: It's seen in gardening girl's hat

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A girl's hat as worn while gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the worm turns up when digging.
explanation.definitionFit: An annelid is a segmented worm such as the earthworm, often seen in garden soil.

clue.text: Wood strip to go in near the end?

definitions.meaning: a long thin strip of timber

definitions.text: to go in near the end?
definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bat at number ten, going in to bat near the end of the order

explanation.surface: A strip of wood is to be fitted at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as BAT TEN: the number ten batter in cricket goes in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A batten is a narrow strip of wood used for fixing or strengthening.

clue.text: Is lively boss part of this group?

indicators.note: lively signals the letters of boss and part jumping about into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether an energetic manager belongs to this team.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'boss' is literally part of the answer group, senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The top brass are the highest-ranking officers or executives, a group to which a boss belongs.

clue.text: Fishing equipment endlessly contains part of fish to process

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a reel is fishing tackle that winds the line
a fin is part of a fish

explanation.surface: Angling gear holding a fish part, ready for processing.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine something is to process it to remove impurities, as with oil or sugar.

clue.text: Remove tops from a certain size of paper mugs

indicators.note: remove signals taking some letters away

parts.note: foolscap is a traditional British paper size
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: An instruction to take the lids off paper cups of a certain size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugs' looks like cups; it means dupes. Foolscap is an old British paper size.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugs is slang for gullible people, which fools also means.

clue.text: Process is mad with only a little ability to make money

indicators.note: to process material is to work it into a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: a touch means a small amount

explanation.surface: A complaint that some process is crazy and earns barely anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas, the mythical king, turned all he touched to gold, so the phrase means a gift for making money.

clue.text: Part of the shield given in the minor league

indicators.note: in shows the letters are lying inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A piece of a trophy shield handed out in a lower sporting division.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an orle is a narrow band forming an inner border on a shield.

clue.text: Writer — poet, not English — one to hang around

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: not shows a letter being left out

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet

explanation.surface: A writer, a poet minus his English, is someone to loiter about.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a jewel hung around the neck on a chain.

clue.text: I love speed when in motion in the event

indicators.note: letters in motion move around, so they are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Fondness for going fast when moving during a happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion' rearranges I, O and SPEED.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is an incident or event in a series of happenings.
